author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read IPS alerts and user activity from the Trellix Intrusion Prevention System Manager (formerly McAfee Network Security Platform). The Manager sends them as syslog to the data collector, using the custom templates in README.md or its default alert message. Alerts go to NIDS and user activity goes to ManagementEvent.
notes:
Setup:
- The Trellix Intrusion Prevention System Manager (formerly McAfee Network Security Platform) sends syslog to the data collector.
- The Manager builds each message from $IV_ variables, and Trellix recommends a custom template, so README.md gives one for IPS alerts and one for user activity, each KEY=value pairs joined by | and starting TRELLIX_IPS=alert| or TRELLIX_IPS=audit|.
- The parser also reads the Manager's default alert message, with fewer fields.

Field mapping:
- Alerts go to NIDS: the attack name as the message, the category as the classification, the attack ID as signature_id, the result as the action with blocked set when it says Blocked, direction, addresses, ports, protocol, application protocol and VLAN.
- Alert ID, severity, confidence, sub-category, detection mechanism, count, interface, domain, MITRE tactic and technique, malware file and hash, and C&C domain go to event_metadata.
- User activity goes to ManagementEvent with the user, action, category, result and message.
- In Sophos NG-SIEM, SPLIT_NAME_VALUES cuts a value at each | and adds the text after it to the value before, so the parent makes each KEY=value pair its own item first, and a user name holding a | stays whole.

Time:
- From 11.1 Update 5 the Manager adds a [Mmm dd, yyyy hh:mm:ss] time to every message; the parser removes it and uses it as the event time, or the syslog time before that release.
- Both are read as UTC.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up from Trellix's variable tables and default message templates.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-15 (106 of 106 fields matched the emulator), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (8 of 8 lines, 106 of 106 fields).
- No built-in parser claimed these lines in 12 Run Tests.
- With a line added whose user name holds a |, Run Test on 2026-10-16 matched all 113 fields with each child combined with the parent (3 of 3 runs) and as a separate parser under it (each line taken in 5 of 5 runs).

Known gaps:
- Faults, firewall access events and quarantine events aren't covered.
- Inside a value, text shaped like a pair (|KEY=) is still read as a pair.
